key_insight: Tev proposes a way to scale long-horizon agent training by turning sparse, hard-to-evaluate tasks into dense-progress learning problems. This gives open-source agents a more practical path to improving on hours- to days-long tasks.
problem_solved: The paper tackles the lack of training data and effective rewards for long-horizon agentic tasks, where success is rare, verification is difficult, and scaling supervision is expensive.
method: Introduce Tev, an environment/training framework designed for long-horizon agentic tasks.
Use dense progress rewards instead of only end-of-task rewards to provide frequent learning signals.
Create a scalable recipe for generating, curating, and verifying complex tasks for agent training.
impact: This matters because it makes long-horizon agent training more feasible for open-source models. Practitioners can potentially build agents that learn more reliably on extended tasks with less dependence on sparse success signals.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing task creation -> execution -> dense reward -> learning loop
Before/after chart comparing sparse rewards vs dense progress rewards
Timeline illustration of short vs long-horizon tasks spanning hours to days
Icon set for task curation, verification, reward shaping, and agent improvement
paper_title: Tev: Scaling Long-Horizon Agentic Environments with Dense Progress Rewards
paper_authors: Wenbo Hu, Shraman Pramanick, Krishna Kumar Singh, Nanyun Peng, Kai-Wei Chang
